rules.title: Minneapolis ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates. Tenants may bring civil actions.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; private civil action

coverage.summary: Citywide prohibition. The available source states no building-size, age or landlord-size limits.

rules.effective_date_note: The effective date of March 1, 2026 comes only from a secondary law-firm alert dated August 21, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 1, 2026. Prohibits algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates; tenants may pursue civil actions.
rules.review_note: The only support is a secondary law-firm alert (Morgan Lewis, August 2026). The official ordinance text was not captured, so these items are unverified: ordinance number, enactment date, definitions, exemptions, penalties and coverage limits. Verify against the official Minneapolis Code.
rules.source_notes: Secondary source: law-firm alert summary table.
